coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic sector is one of the entities that may keep the old 10% INSS rate (4% worker, 6% employer) only with INSS authorization, under DL 1/2025 (third amendment of DL 19/2022). No evidence of an online filing portal or of mandatory domestic-worker registration. Weak candidate C1.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One combined query (sucata, ferro velho, ouro) returned nothing for STP. No licensing regime or register found. Consistent with K05.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No dedicated search. No sources surfaced incidentally.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Covered only by the combined scrap/gold query: nothing on STP. No gold-dealer regime found; no gold mining sector to speak of.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Budget. No sources surfaced.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: DL 06/2019 (DR I Série n.º 46, 14 Aug 2019) regulates import, export and trade of live animals and animal products (FAOLEX sao196904). Detailed licence and reporting duties not read. Candidate C6.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No STP abattoir or butcher licensing text found; only DL 06/2019 on trade in animal products. Imported beef is small (Portugal about USD 135k in 2023).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget. No sources surfaced.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Same query as 6/7: nothing on vet practices or vet medicine sellers beyond DL 06/2019.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Budget. No sources surfaced.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Budget. Only tangential: the Lei de Base do Ambiente was amended by Lei 7/2026 and a National Environment Agency was created by DL 04/2026 (see 32).

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Budget. No sources surfaced; near-zero lift stock expected on the islands (unverified).

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: AGER regulates telecom, postal, water and electricity (trade.gov guide). EMAE runs about 16 mostly gravity-fed systems. No AGER licensing text or community water-committee rules found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Budget. Only a 2015 draft plant-health decree-law (CIAT-STP, ippc.int) surfaced; adoption not confirmed.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Labour Code is Lei 6/2019. Rules on foreign workers and national quotas are mentioned, but the final text and any permit portal were not found.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Budget. No sources surfaced.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: FONG-STP federation has over 200 NGO members (Forus). 2010 ordinance extended immediate association set-up to several registries. Churches, private social solidarity institutions and non-profits can keep the 10% INSS rate by authorization. No annual reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. A 2017 academic paper describes informal motoqueiros. The Road Code dated to 1954, and a new code was proposed (adoption unverified). No taxi or moto-taxi licensing regime found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. INSS director estimates about 70% of the workforce is informal, mainly transport, fishing and trade (Forbes Africa Lusófona).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Budget. No sources surfaced.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: ENCO holds the import and sale monopoly for petroleum products (older academic source). DERCAE (Direcção de Regulação e Controlo das Actividades Económicas) found fuel-pump fraud and set fines of 20,000 to 200,000 dobras (undated news). No licensing decree found. Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: 2023 exports: cocoa about USD 10M, crude palm oil about USD 5.5M, pepper about USD 254k. Agripalma plant opened Dec 2019. Exporter licence and phytosanitary procedure not found. Cocoa EUDR is already covered by K02 and K04.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: CECAB (42 associations, about 3,000 growers) and CECAQ-11 export about 40% of cocoa. Microfinance and payment-institution licensing notices from the Banco Central were not found. UNCDF Payment Infrastructure Assessment (April 2025) is the likeliest source and was not read.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Lei 9/2018 (health bases) recognises private and mixed providers. The ADS (state employee health scheme) contract with private clinics was not found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: No STP pharmacy or medicine-import licensing text found; only Timor-Leste and Angola results, which were ignored.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No private security regime found. General INSS duties: 12% rate from 1 Jan 2025 (7% employer, 5% employee) under DL 1/2025. Payroll vendors (Ontop, Playroll) serve foreign employers only.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Lei 9/2020 of 22 Sep 2020 governs extraction of aggregates: coastal sand extraction is banned with exceptions, and licences come from the natural resources ministry. Informal beach sand extraction is widespread, and a World Bank-backed roadmap exists (Ceris, Aug 2024). No contractor alvará regime found. Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AML law is Lei 8/2013 of 15 Oct 2013; the FIU (UIF) was created by DL 60/2009. The GIABA/FATF mutual evaluation was adopted in Nov 2024 (on-site June 2023). The report page returned HTTP 403, so DNFBP coverage is unverified. Candidate C5.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: A tourist tax of about EUR 2.10 per person per day is paid at hotels (2024 travel brochure, unverified); an older report says EUR 3.10. A 2016 tourism bill said the sector lacked a legal framework; no current accommodation licensing or guest-register decree found. Visitors reached about 41k in 2024. Candidate C8.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Cocoa is covered by K02 and K04. Vanilla, pepper and palm oil exporters: phytosanitary certificate model exists on IPPC, but the 2015 plant-health decree-law draft was not confirmed adopted. See C10.

coverage.category: 31. Fisheries: artisanal fisher, palaiê and vessel registry under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Law
coverage.found: Lei 09/2022 (DR 22 June 2022) replaced Lei 9/2001. The EU-STP protocol expired 22 May 2018 and talks were suspended. Artisanal licence and vessel registration procedure not found. Same buyer group and duty as K01.

coverage.category: 32. Environmental licensing: Lei 7/2026 and the new National Environment Agency
coverage.found: Lei 7/2026 of 13 Aug 2026 amended and republished the Lei de Base do Ambiente (in force 18 Aug 2026). DL 04/2026 created the Agência Nacional do Ambiente. The licensing and EIA procedure text was not found. Candidate C7.

coverage.category: 33. Payments and mobile money agents, fintechs, Banco Central licensing
coverage.found: Over 70% of people pay by mobile phone (BCSTP governor). The RTGS system was to go live in 2024, and SIBS runs Dobra24. GolFinTech says it has been licensed since 2021. No agent or reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 34. Social security (INSS) contribution regime changes
coverage.found: DL 1/2025 of 7 Jan 2025 raised the rate to 12% from 1 Jan 2025, with payments due Feb 2025. The old 10% rate is kept only with INSS authorization for churches, private social solidarity institutions, firms with turnover up to 90 UCSS (about STN 108,000), the domestic sector and non-profits. Employers hiring young first-job seekers can be exempt for up to a year. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 35. Petroleum service-provider registration with ANP-STP
coverage.found: DL 22/2022 of 14 Sep 2022 set registration for service providers with ANP-STP, in force 1 Jan 2023 (Miranda alert). The duty falls mainly on larger or foreign firms; the small local share is unverified. Weak candidate C9.

coverage.category: 36. Business registration and VAT (IVA) for small taxpayers
coverage.found: Registration goes through the Guiché Único (Ministry of Justice), mostly in person (Deel guide, unverified). IVA took effect 1 June 2023 per 2025 and 2026 academic sources, while a 2019 law firm note gave 1 March 2020. E-invoicing is not found for STP. Covered by K03.

candidates.buyer: COOPAPIP (cooperative, about 31 members) / Príncipe regional government
candidates.known_note: Buyer is a single small cooperative; far below viable market size.
candidates.name: Príncipe certified-honey cooperative register (COOPAPIP) and bee-protection compliance
candidates.trigger: Regional bee-protection law drafted 2017 with COOPAPIP: bans hive burning and selling honey unless by a certified cooperative member. Number, text and current status not found.
candidates.unchecked: Law number and text; whether certification involves recurring filings; cooperative current size; any budget to pay.

candidates.buyer: Importers/sellers of plants, plant products and agro-inputs
candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.known_note: Overlaps loosely with K02 only through cocoa exports; different duty (inputs/plant health), not EUDR.
candidates.name: Phytosanitary and agro-input dealer/importer compliance under DL 5/2016 (CIAT)
candidates.trigger: Decreto-Lei 5/2016 Plant Health Framework Act (CIAT-STP authority); Decreto 40/99 phytosanitary certificates for exports; adoption of the 2015 draft now confirmed as DL 5/2016.
candidates.unchecked: Whether dealer licensing, pesticide registers or applicator certificates exist; number of dealers; whether CIAT permits are paper-based. Probably only a few dozen importers or agro-dealers.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Two searches (second-hand/scrap licensing; pawnshops) found no STP-specific licensing or register regime for second-hand dealers or pawnbrokers. Only tangential: Decree-Law 13/2010 (National Payments System) and Law 9/2010 (AML/CFT amendment) exist but are not tied to pawnshops. Nothing new beyond K05 (informal registers rejected).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No STP rules on dismantlers, scrap vehicles or used parts found. Vehicle import is said (commercial source, unverified) to have an age limit for used cars; no instrument found. Road Code: Lei 04/IX/11 (new Código de Estrada, final text Feb 2013, replacing the 1954 code) exists; no periodic-inspection or dismantler provisions seen. Roughly USD 5.6M cars imported in 2022 (tradingeconomics, secondary). No candidate.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Sector is tiny (2015 thesis: about 3 beekeepers on STP island). Only regulated niche is Príncipe: regional bee-protection law drafted 2017 bans burning hives and selling honey unless by a certified COOPAPIP member (cooperative founded 2016, 31 members, Ponta do Sol). Law number and current status unverified. Too small and cooperative-run for software; listed as a weak candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Lei 07/2018 Lei-Quadro dos Recursos Hídricos (DR 55, 2 May 2018, in force 26 May 2018) found at ampeid.org and FAOLEX, but I could not read licence/permit articles or any implementing decree (summary page silent; FAOLEX PDF unreadable). No driller register or abstraction-permit workflow confirmed. Unchecked: Lei 07/2018 full text.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No STP law on septic tanks or desludging found. Academic sources (2025 dissertation, UNILAB, Lusófona) describe open dumping and weak institutions; PNGIRSU (national solid-waste plan) mentioned without approval status. DL 14/2003 covers packaging waste only. Tangential items already in the gap note: Lei 7/2026 and DL 04/2026 (National Environment Agency). No candidate.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Search returned no STP regime for lifts, boilers or pressure vessels (only Brazil NR-13 and Ontario TSSA). Nothing suggests a statutory inspection scheme. Near-zero lift stock remains an unverified assumption. Not a candidate.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Update to the gap note: the plant-health framework was adopted as Decreto-Lei 5/2016 (Plant Health Framework Act, 88 articles, 8 chapters, 9 annexes), naming CIAT-STP as competent authority and binding public and private parties that produce, import, export or sell plants and plant products (FAOLEX summary via leap.unep.org, page 403 on fetch, summary only via search). Also Decreto 40/99 (CIAT phytosanitary border control, phytosanitary certificates for exports) and Decreto 20/2010 (phytosanitary agreement with Cape Verde). No pesticide registration, dealer licensing or applicator certification instrument found. No candidate; CIAT border permits are small-volume and state-run.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No STP law, municipal cemetery regulation or funeral-agency licensing found in two searches (results were Portugal, Brazil, Cape Verde). Cemeteries likely run by distrital councils (unverified). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: Road Code Lei 04/IX/11 (2013) consulted driving-school representatives; DTT (Direcção dos Transportes Terrestres) is the authority; no school licensing or student-register rules seen. Nurseries: no STP instrument found. Food: Decreto-Lei 19/2011 (food safety, Codex-aligned, 10 June 2011) exists but licensing articles unread. Tattoo and hunting: no sources, assumed negligible. No candidate.
